confidence_note: Book not read; study details are from Goleman's later reprint of the same research and from the publisher's reader's guide. The old 'common blind spots' list is replaced by the guide's list. No invented leader scene.
facts: Goleman cites studies in which accurate self-assessment marked superior performance: several hundred managers from twelve organizations, and several hundred knowledge workers (computer scientists, auditors) at companies such as AT&T and 3M, where it appeared in nearly every star performer.
On 360-degree assessments, average performers tend to overestimate their strengths; star performers rarely do, and often underestimate their abilities, which Goleman links to high internal standards.
A deficit in accurate self-assessment can act as a career derailer.

The reader's guide lists blind spots that block self-awareness: blind ambition, unrealistic goals, relentless striving, drives others, power hungry, insatiable need for recognition, preoccupation with appearances, need to seem perfect.
The guide also says: 'We need time to be introspective, but we don't get it - or don't take it.'
Goleman describes financial planners whose emotional self-awareness helped them manage their own reactions when discussing mortality in life insurance sales.

Goleman cites self-confidence evidence: in a study of 112 entry-level accountants, self-efficacy predicted supervisor ratings ten months later more strongly than skill or prior training; in a sixty-year study of more than 1,000 high-IQ people, early self-confidence predicted career success.
tension: The average performers rate themselves highly and the stars rate themselves lower.
opening_idea: Stars who underestimate themselves while average performers overestimate.

lessons.idea: Ask people who work with you to rate you on the same scale as you rate yourself, and look at the gap.

reflect_final: Who around you would give you an honest rating on one skill, and what would you ask them to score?

use_cases.move: Rate yourself on three skills, ask a colleague to do the same, and compare.

use_cases.situation: A one-on-one with a direct report
use_cases.move: Ask which of your habits makes their work harder, and listen without defending.
Ask a sibling or partner which of your habits they would change, and thank them.

pocket_idea: Stars rate themselves lower than average performers do: ask someone to score you before you score yourself.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: In Goleman's data the average performers overrate themselves and the stars often underrate themselves.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Goleman cites studies where accurate self-assessment marked star performers; on 360 ratings averages overestimated and stars sometimes underestimated.
